title: Sort the Matrix Diagonally
summary: Define a matrix diagonal as a line of cells starting from any cell in the top row or left column and extending diagonally to the bottom-right.
statement: Define a matrix diagonal as a line of cells starting from any cell in the top row or left column and extending diagonally to the bottom-right. Given an m x n matrix of integers, sort each diagonal in ascending order and return the modified matrix.
constraints: Sort each top-left to bottom-right diagonal independently in ascending order.
hints: Cells share a diagonal exactly when i-j is equal.
Group values by i-j and sort each group in reverse order.
Traverse row-major and pop the smallest remaining value for that diagonal.
Each group is independently written in increasing traversal order.
editorial: Each group is independently written in increasing traversal order.

tests.explanation: Each i-j diagonal is sorted and written back from top-left to bottom-right.
